claims.text: Cast and annealed CoCrFeMnNi can serve as a single-phase FCC high-entropy-alloy baseline with coarse grains and minimal precipitate formation.
Applying approximately 30% cold rolling increases dislocation density.
Subsolvus aging at approximately 600–700°C can nucleate and stabilize nanoscale precipitates within grains.
Subsolvus aging at approximately 600–700°C can nucleate and stabilize nanoscale precipitates along grain boundaries.
The combined deformation and aging route will refine the alloy's grains.
The combined route will produce a uniform network of nanoscale precipitates.
Cold-work-induced dislocations serve as precipitate-nucleation sites during aging.
The nanoscale precipitates strengthen the alloy by obstructing dislocation motion.
The precipitates stabilize grain boundaries.
Grain refinement and stable precipitate interfaces promote more uniform plastic deformation.
More uniform plastic deformation increases ductility.
More uniform plastic deformation increases fracture resistance.
The precipitates will not cause a significant loss of Young's modulus.
Slight stiffening of the matrix by the precipitates will modestly increase Young's modulus.
The proposed processing route will increase yield strength and ultimate strength by approximately 15–25% relative to the untreated as-cast or annealed baseline.
The proposed processing route will increase Young's modulus by approximately 5–10% relative to the untreated baseline.
The proposed processing route will improve ductility relative to the untreated baseline.
The proposed processing route will improve fracture toughness relative to the untreated baseline.
Excessive aging can coarsen precipitates and negate the anticipated property improvements.
Excessive deformation can produce work hardening and embrittlement that negate the anticipated property improvements.
